## What

One paragraph: what this change does and why. One concern per PR.

## Test-first checklist

The reviewer is checking for the culture, not just the code:

- [ ] The failing test came first — it is in this PR (or, for a bug fix, the
      existing test that now pins the behaviour is named) and it failed for
      the right reason before the fix.
- [ ] Fixtures are snapshots of real pre-change behaviour, not values
      generated by the new code.
- [ ] The whole suite ran and is green:
      - [ ] iOS: `xcodebuild test` for the touched framework (see
            `DEVELOPER.md`), or "not applicable — no Apple target touched".
      - [ ] Linux: `./Linux/build.sh` when anything the Linux build compiles
            was touched (`Linux/cmake/*Sources.cmake`), or "not applicable".
- [ ] New `NEED` divergences carry a reason; nothing is silently skipped.
- [ ] New files carry the SPDX header; deliberately-unused code is marked
      with the clang attribute, not an unmarked warning.
- [ ] A `BUGS.md` fix moves its entry to `BUGS_FIXED.md` with the test named.

## Commit sign-off

- [ ] Every commit ends with `Signed-off-by:` (DCO — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

## Notes for the reviewer

Anything that will help: the commit-by-commit story, the design trade-off,
what you deliberately did not do.
